assumptions.choice: Per bar, check stop-loss breach first, then the opposite RSI cross, then EOD liquidation time; only the first true condition triggers the close.
assumptions.reason: Spec lists the stop-loss as a separately-checked-each-bar rule, then states the cross/EOD exit as 'whichever comes first'; when multiple conditions coincide on one bar an explicit priority is needed and stop-loss (risk control) is given precedence.

assumptions.choice: Stop breach is tested against the bar's Low (long) or High (short) rather than Close only.
assumptions.reason: Only OHLCV bar data is available (no tick/order-book data); using High/Low is the closest literal reading of a price level 'checked each bar' with a fixed percentage stop.

assumptions.choice: 09:30-16:00 session bounds are declared as parameters but not used to filter bars.
assumptions.reason: The supplied data feed already contains only regular-session 15m bars, so no additional session filtering logic is applied; the times are still defined per the spec.

assumptions.choice: Entries/exits use plain self.buy()/self.sell()/self.close() market orders, filled at the next bar's open per backtrader's default broker behavior.
assumptions.reason: Canonical defaults specify plain orders for unstated sizing/closing; no stop-order or same-bar-fill mechanism was specified, so no override of the environment's default fill timing was introduced.

assumptions.choice: If a position exits before 13:30 while the day's classified trend and midday window are still active, a new entry on a subsequent qualifying RSI cross is allowed.
assumptions.reason: The spec restricts entries only by 'one position at a time' and 'no new entries after 13:30'; it does not state a one-trade-per-day limit, so none was added.

assumptions.choice: The 11:30 trend classification (and SMA[-4] lookback) only evaluates once len(self) >= sma_period + trend_lookback bars exist; days without enough history simply get morning_trend=None (no trade).
assumptions.reason: Backtrader's automatic minperiod (max of SMA(20) and RSI(14)) governs when next() first runs; the extra length guard prevents indexing sma[-4] before it is valid, consistent with relying on automatic warm-up rather than manual bar-skipping.
